I farm 16.1 mu here in Quzhou. I keep about 3 mu for cotton on the drier plot near the road, and the other 13.1 mu runs wheat-maize double crop like most everyone around here. My wife and I handle the daily work, kids send money from the city but they don't come back for planting.

For wheat, I plant Jimai 22 again — it did alright last year, about 480 kg per mu, and my neighbor Old Wang got 500. I buy compound fertilizer 15-15-15, two bags (100 kg) per mu at sowing, then topdress with urea at green-up, one bag (50 kg) per mu. That gives me roughly 18 kg N, 15 kg P, 15 kg K. I water four times — before winter, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. The well runs fine. Spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew, maybe three times if the weather is wet.

For maize after wheat, I go with Zhengdan 958, a hybrid everyone trusts. No-till seeding right into the wheat stubble saves me labor and diesel. One bag compound at planting and one bag urea at big flare stage, about 20 kg N total. I only water once or twice in July if it's dry — the summer rain usually helps. Spray once for armyworm, once for stem borer.

For cotton, I stick with the Bt hybrid from the dealer in town. Cotton eats more potash so I put on 15 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K. Plough the cotton land before planting — cotton likes deep soil. Three irrigations through the season. Cotton always needs more spraying — four or five times for aphids, bollworm, spider mites. It's work but the price this year looks okay.

I am spending more on fertilizer than some say is needed, but I'd rather have a full harvest than save 100 yuan and lose 50 kg of grain. That's how I've always done it.
